classification_signals: Abstract: 'This research investigated the extent to which building occupants’ sense of well-being changed in response to varying daylight levels under Daylight and Daylight plus View conditions... A thesis submitted in fulfilment of the requirements for the degree of Doctor of Philosophy'
Abstract: 'The laboratory cohort was comprised of 20 young... and 18 elderly... adults. Significant associations between light and heart rate variability (HRV) were found.'
Abstract: 'An online survey was conducted separately to collect further data on building occupants’ lighting preferences.'
Chapter 4: 'Method Review, Experiment Design and Procedure' details the quantitative laboratory study.
Chapter 9: 'Lighting condition preference online survey' details the qualitative and quantitative survey component.
Chapter 3: 'Review of standards, codes, guidelines and ordinances that regulate daylighting requirements' indicates a review component.
title: The impact of nonvisual effects of daylight on building occupants: Implications on lighting standards and human centric lighting design

findings.quote: Significant associations between light and heart rate variability (HRV) were found.

findings.antecedent: Bright outdoor daylight exposure (higher light intensity)
findings.quote: The HF Power... was observed when the participants were exposed to bright outdoor daylight (HFnu outdoor: 31.0 ± 1.2 versus HFnu indoor: 30.2 ± 1.2).

The HF power was found to be positively correlated with the light intensity, t(43.6) = -2.21, p = 0.03, supporting the hypothesis that an increase in the level of sense of well-being accompanied the increase in lighting.

The online survey showed that respondents were proportionally happier, Ρ(73) = 0.25, p = 0.03, more energetic, Ρ(73) = 0.24, p = 0.04, and less tense, Ρ(73) = -0.30, p = 0.01, when they were satisfied with their lighting environment.

findings.consequent: Changes in HRV measures, Changes in psychological markers
findings.quote: neither changes in the HRV measures nor the psychological markers had any significant association with the changes in salivary cortisol levels Table 7.8.

The positive correlation between mel – EDI and salivary cortisol was consistent with studies that showed bright light (with short wavelength blue light) altered the photoentrainment of our circadian rhythm, i.e., elevation of cortisol and suppression of melatonin expression.
The HF power, which is associated with vagal modulation (slowing) of the HR, was negatively correlated with salivary cortisol.

This pilot study illustrated that even insignificant changes in lighting could potentially affect cortisol expression. The effect was restricted to the short wavelength, melanopic EDI (mel – EDI), and correlated colour temperature (CCT) components of the light measures.
The current lighting standard unit of measure... photopic illuminance lux... did not affect the salivary cortisol in this small sample study.
